titulo: One Week to Dance More, Phone in Your Pocket
caption:
One Week to Dance More, Phone in Your Pocket

The songwriter Dani Offline asks how her life would change if she danced more and listened more, instead of talking. Here is one way to try it, as a week: Wednesday, listen to a friend talk, all the way through. Friday, send a friend a song you love, and ask them to come dancing. Saturday, keep the phone in your pocket and dance among other people.

To us, taking part, sharing with others, that very simple thing in life, is spiritual, because we are all connected. Who could you take dancing this week?

From "everyone wants to be a DJ, no one wants to dance" by Dani Offline, offline soul, 11 Sep 2025: https://danioffline.substack.com/p/everyone-wants-to-be-a-dj-no-one . Her line "sharing, slowing, watching myself disappear" is quoted as hers. The week, the sentence about taking part and the question are ours: our words, our view. Dani Offline did not make or endorse this video. Her essay and every NAOS strategy are on the NAOS page linked in our bio.

More strategies: link in bio.

alt: Pencil animation of a weekly spread on a sketchbook page, "monday to sunday" lettered at the top. On each day a red pencil first draws an output, such as a notebook of notes or a phone held up filming. An eraser rubs each one out and leaves a pink ghost. Graphite draws the shared version instead. Two people share one speech bubble, then two people share earphones. On Saturday a crowd of bodies dances, with a phone-shaped bump in one pocket. Small figures on every day are joined by graphite lines. Captions follow the voice, with "our words, our view" on our sentence. At the end the pencil writes her words "sharing, slowing, watching myself disappear" across the whole week. End card: who could you take dancing this week? and the credit.
